source_text:
ἕκαστα διαστείχοντες, τὰ εἰκότα λέγωμεν· Δώσομεν γὰρ σοφοῖς ἀφορμὴν, καὶ γνωριοῦμεν δικαίοις, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον. Προσθεῖεν δ' ἂν καὶ αὐτοὶ τὰ παρά γε δὴ σφῶν αὐτῶν, καὶ ἀμείνους ἔσονται παρὰ πολύ.
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ μάλα.
{ΚΥΡ.} Οὐκοῦν ἐν ἔτους ἀρχῇ καὶ ἐν πρώτῳ μηνὶ, τὸ Χριστοῦ μυστήριον ἐκφαίνεται· νέος γὰρ ἡμῖν αἰὼν, ὁ τῆς τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν ἐπιδημίας καιρὸς, μετατιθεὶς ἅπαντα πρὸς τὸ ἄμεινον, καὶ εἰς καινότητα κτίσεως μεταστοιχειῶν εὖ μάλα, τὸ παλαιούμενον καὶ γηράσκον, καὶ ἐγγὺς ἀφανισμοῦ. «Καινὴ γὰρ κτίσις, τὰ ἐν Χριστῷ, καὶ τὰ ἀρχαῖα παρῆλθεν, ἰδοὺ γέγονε τὰ πάντα καινά.» Ζῶμεν δὲ καὶ ἡμεῖς, οὐκέτι Μωσαϊκῶς, ἀπενηνεγμένοι δὲ μᾶλλον εἰς εὐαγγελικὴν ζωὴν, καινουργοῦντος ἡμᾶς διὰ Πνεύματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὀρθῶς ἔφης.
{ΚΥΡ.} Ἕκαστος δὲ λαμβάνει τὸ πρόβατον, καὶ συλλέγονται κατὰ πληθὺν οἱ δαιτυμόνες εἰς οἶκον ἕνα. Μεμερισμένοι γὰρ ὥσπερ καὶ ἡμεῖς εἰς τὸ ὑφεστάναι καθ' ἕνα φυσικῶς, εἰς ἑνότητα τὴν πνευματικὴν συνδεδραμήκαμεν ἐν Χριστῷ. Ψυχὴ γὰρ ἐν ἡμῖν λοιπόν ἐστι μία, καὶ καρδία μία. Πρόβατον δὲ τὸ θυόμενον, ἤγουν ἐξ αἰγῶν, καὶ πρόβατον μὲν, διά τοι τὸ ἀσυγκρίτως ἥμερόν τε καὶ ἄκακον, καὶ πρός γε δὴ τούτῳ τὸ ἔγκαρπον· «Ὡς πρόβατον γὰρ ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη, καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἐναντίον τοῦ κείροντος αὐτὸν ἄφωνος.» Ἀμνὸς δὲ, ὅτι τέθυται δι' ἡμᾶς, καὶ ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν παρεδόθη, κατὰ τὰς Γραφάς. Ἔριφος δὲ ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτιῶν τὸ θῦμα, κατὰ τὸν νόμον, τέλειόν τε ἄρσεν τὸ πρόβατον· τοῦ μὲν τελείου σημαίνοντος, ἤτοι τὸ μώμου παντὸς ἐλεύθερον, εὔρωστόν τε καὶ ὑγιές. Ἄμωμος γὰρ Χριστὸς, καὶ παντὸς ἐπέκεινα πάθους, ἤτοι τὸ τέλειον ἀληθῶς· παντέλειος γὰρ ὁ Ἐμμανουὴλ, οἴκοθεν ἔχων καὶ φυσικῶς, τὰ δι' ὧν ἐστι Θεὸς, τοῦ γε μὴν ἄρσενος ὅτι πάντων ἐστὶ καθηγητής. Ἡγεμονικώτατον δὲ τὸ ἄρσεν ἀεὶ, καὶ ἐν δευτέρᾳ τάξει τὸ θῆλυ πανταχῆ. Καὶ λαμβάνεται μὲν τὸ πρόβατον, ἀπὸ δεκάτης τοῦ μηνός· ἱερουργεῖται δὲ πρὸς ἑσπέραν τῇ τεσσαρεσκαιδεκάτῃ. Οὐ γάρ τοι νεοφανὲς τὸ Χριστοῦ μυστήριον, οὐδὲ τότε πρῶτον διεγνωσμένον, ὅτε καὶ ἐμπαροινεῖν ἐδόκει τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις αὐτῷ. Ἀρχαιοτέρα δὲ πολὺ τοῦ πάθους ἡ γνῶσις προῆν, προαναφωνούντων ἁγίων, καὶ διακεκραγότος τοῦ νόμου, καὶ τὸ ἐπ' αὐτῷ μυστήριον, τῆς ἁγίας ἡμῖν προανατυπούσης Γραφῆς. Οὐκοῦν εἴχομεν παρ' ἑαυτοῖς ὡς ἐν προγνώσει τέως, τεθυμένον μὲν οὔπω τὸν ἀμνὸν, σφαγήσεται δὲ ὅτι πρὸς ἑσπέραν, οὐκ ἠγνοηκότες. Ἐπ' ἐσχάτοις γὰρ τοῦ αἰῶνος καιροῖς, καὶ πρὸς αὐταῖς ἤδη πως διήκοντος ταῖς τοῦ χρόνου δυσμαῖς ὁ Χριστοῦ πέπρακται θάνατος. Σφάζεται δὲ ὑπὸ παντὸς τοῦ πλήθους· ἀπέθανε γὰρ ὑπὲρ πάντων, ἵν' εἰδεῖεν οὗτοι ὑπὲρ τῆς ἑαυτῶν σωτηρίας προσάγοντες ἀμνὸν, ὅτι τιμῆς ἠγοράσθησαν, οὐκ εἰσὶν ἑαυτῶν, ἀλλ' εἷς ὑπὲρ πάντων ἀπέθανεν, ἵνα οἱ ζῶντες μηκέτι ἑαυτοῖς ζῶσιν, ἀλλὰ τῷ ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν ἀποθανόντι, καὶ ἐγερθέντι. Ἐπειδὴ γὰρ
pass_a_gloss: (… finely and in passing) going through each thing, let us say the likely things; for we will give occasion to wise men and will make known to righteous men, according to what is written. And they themselves would add the things from themselves, and they will be better by much. PALL.: Very much so. CYR.: Therefore at the beginning of the year and in the first month the mystery of Christ is shown forth; for a new age (is) for us, the season of the sojourn of our Savior, transferring all things toward the better, and transforming very well into newness of creation the thing growing old and aging and near disappearance. 'For the things in Christ (are) a new creation, and the ancient things passed away; behold all things have become new.' And we too live no longer Mosaically, but having been carried away rather into evangelical life, Christ renewing us through the Spirit. PALL.: You spoke rightly. CYR.: And each takes the sheep, and the feasters are gathered in multitude into one house. For we too, having been divided as it were into subsisting one by one naturally, have run together into the spiritual unity in Christ. For one soul is in us from now on, and one heart. And the thing sacrificed (is) a sheep, or rather from goats; and a sheep on account of the incomparably tame and innocent, and besides this the fruitful: 'for as a sheep he was led to slaughter, and as a lamb before the one shearing him, voiceless.' And a lamb, because he has been sacrificed through us and was handed over for our sins according to the Scriptures. And a kid (is) the victim for sins according to the law; and the sheep perfect, male: the perfect signifying the being free from every blemish, robust and healthy; for Christ (is) blameless and beyond every passion, that is, the truly perfect; for Emmanuel (is) all-perfect, having from himself and naturally the things through which he is God; and the male (signifying) that he is leader of all; for the male is always most governing, and the female in second rank everywhere. And the sheep is taken from the tenth of the month, but it is sacrificed toward evening on the fourteenth. For the mystery of Christ is not newly appeared, nor first recognized then, when it seemed (good) to the Jews also to behave drunkenly against him. But the knowledge went before, much older than the suffering, the saints foretelling, and the law crying out, and the holy Scripture prefiguring for us the mystery about him. Therefore we had it among ourselves as in foreknowledge meanwhile, the lamb not yet sacrificed, but not being ignorant that it will be slaughtered toward evening. For at the last seasons of the age, and (time) already somehow reaching to the very settings of time, the death of Christ was accomplished. And it is slaughtered by all the multitude; for he died on behalf of all, so that these, bringing the lamb for their own salvation, might know that they were bought with a price, they are not their own, but one died on behalf of all, so that those living no longer live to themselves but to the one who died on their behalf and was raised. For since (continues).
pass_b_english: Cyril: …going through each point, should we say what is fitting? For we will ‘give the wise an occasion, and make things known to the righteous,’ as it is written (Proverbs 9:9); and they too may add what is their own, and they will be far better for it.

Cyril: Well then, at the beginning of the year and in the first month the mystery of Christ is revealed. For a new age has come to us, the time of our Savior's coming among us, which changes all things for the better and very well refashions into a newness of creation what was growing old and aging and near to vanishing (Hebrews 8:13). ‘For the things in Christ are a new creation; the old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new’ (2 Corinthians 5:17). And we ourselves live no longer in the manner of Moses; we have been carried over, rather, into the life of the gospel, since Christ makes us new through the Spirit.

Cyril: Each man takes the sheep, and the diners gather in numbers into one house. For we too, divided as we are by nature into separate existence one by one, have run together into spiritual unity in Christ; for from now on there is one soul in us, and one heart (Acts 4:32). The victim is a sheep, or else one from the goats. A sheep, because of its incomparable gentleness and innocence, and besides this its fruitfulness: ‘For he was led as a sheep to the slaughter, and as a lamb before its shearer is silent’ (Isaiah 53:7). A lamb, because he was sacrificed for us and handed over for our sins, according to the Scriptures. A kid, because by the law that is the sacrifice offered for sins. The sheep is perfect and male. ‘Perfect’ signifies that it is free from every blemish, strong and healthy; for Christ is without blemish and beyond every passion, which is to say truly perfect, since Emmanuel is all-perfect, having of himself and by nature all that makes him God. ‘Male’ signifies that he is the leader of all; for the male is always the more governing, and the female everywhere in the second rank.

The sheep is taken from the tenth of the month, but it is offered toward evening on the fourteenth. For the mystery of Christ is not newly come to light, nor was it first recognized when the Jews thought fit to treat him with drunken violence. The knowledge of it went far ahead of the suffering, since the saints foretold it, the law cried it aloud, and Holy Scripture sketched in advance for us the mystery concerning him. So for the time being we held it among ourselves as foreknowledge: the lamb not yet sacrificed, but we were not unaware that it would be slaughtered toward evening. For it was in the last times of the age, when time was already somehow reaching its very setting, that the death of Christ was accomplished. And it is slaughtered by the whole multitude, for he died for all; so that those who offer the lamb for their own salvation may know that they were bought with a price and are not their own (1 Corinthians 6:19–20), but that ‘one died for all, so that those who live might no longer live for themselves, but for him who died for them and was raised’ (2 Corinthians 5:14–15). For since…

choices.english: or else one from the goats
choices.why: Exodus 12:5 allows lambs or kids; ἤγουν here gives the alternative.
Moral sense (free of passion), set beside 'without blemish'.

choices.english: have run together into spiritual unity in Christ
choices.why: The old English printed 'gathered into one house — the Church — and feast together on one Christ', which is not in the Greek.
